changes.text: 蔺相如从渑池回来，因功拜为上卿，位次排在廉颇之上。廉颇是赵国良将，伐齐取阳晋，以勇气闻名诸侯，他的态度很直接：蔺相如「徒以口舌爲勞」，凭什么位居我上。他公开放话，见了面就要羞辱对方。这件事难在，按他自己的说法，他有攻城野战之大功，而相如的功劳记在口舌上，两人同朝为上卿，一个要辱，一个在躲。

Lin Xiangru came back from the meeting at Mianchi and was made shangqing, placed above Lian Po. Lian Po was a fine general of Zhao: he had beaten Qi, taken Yangjin and won a name for courage among the states. His reaction was blunt. Lin Xiangru had earned his place with nothing but his tongue; why should he sit above me? He announced that the next time they met he would humiliate the man. What makes the episode hard is that, by Lian Po's own account, he had great merit from storming cities and fighting in the field, while Lin Xiangru's credit was entered under words. Now both held the rank of shangqing at court: one meant to humiliate, the other hid.
廉颇的资历是战场上打出来的：赵惠文王时为赵将伐齐，大破之，取阳晋，拜为上卿。蔺相如的来历则完全不同——他是赵国人，身份是宦者令缪贤的舍人，也就是门客。后来廉颇不服时，说的理由之一正是相如「素賤人」。

Lian Po's credentials were earned on the battlefield. In the reign of King Huiwen of Zhao he commanded against Qi, routed it, seized Yangjin, and was raised to shangqing. Lin Xiangru's origins could hardly have been more different. He was a man of Zhao, and his standing was that of a sheren - a retainer in the service of Miao Xian, the head of the palace eunuchs. When Lian Po later refused to accept him, one of the reasons he gave was exactly this: the man had always been of low station.

赵惠文王时，赵国得到楚国的和氏璧，秦昭王写信来，说愿用十五座城换它。赵王与大将军廉颇诸大臣商量，两头都难：给，怕城拿不到，白白被骗；不给，又怕秦兵打过来。主意定不下来，缺一个能去秦国回话的人。缪贤向赵王提起相如，讲了自己的一桩旧事：他曾有罪，私下打算逃去燕国，相如劝住他，理由是赵强燕弱、他正得宠于赵王，燕王当年示好正因为此，逃过去只会被捆着送回来；不如「肉袒伏斧質請罪」，倒还有活路。缪贤照做，赵王果然赦免了他。

In King Huiwen's time Zhao acquired the Heshi jade from Chu, and King Zhaoxiang of Qin wrote offering fifteen cities for it. The king of Zhao consulted his great general Lian Po and the other ministers, and both answers looked bad: hand it over and the cities might never come, leaving Zhao cheated; refuse, and Qin's armies might come. Nothing was settled, and there was no one fit to carry the reply to Qin. Miao Xian brought up Lin Xiangru with the king, telling a story against himself. He had once been guilty of an offence and meant to flee to Yan. Lin Xiangru stopped him: Zhao was strong and Yan weak, and the king of Yan had courted Miao Xian only because he stood in the king of Zhao's favour; flee there, and Yan would tie him up and send him back. Better to bare his upper body, lie down at the executioner's block and ask pardon (to paraphrase the source) - there might still be a way to keep his life. Miao Xian did, and the king pardoned him.
《史记》记有这样的权衡：秦以城求璧而赵不许，理亏在赵；赵给了璧而秦不给城，理亏在秦。「均之二策，甯許以負秦曲」——两相比较，宁可答应，让理亏落到秦国头上。相如奉璧出使秦国。

The Shiji records this weighing of options. If Qin offers cities for the jade and Zhao refuses, the wrong is Zhao's; if Zhao hands over the jade and Qin refuses the cities, the wrong is Qin's. Weighing the two courses together, it is better to agree and leave Qin carrying the blame. Lin Xiangru went to Qin as envoy with the jade.

到了秦廷，秦王在章台接见相如，接过璧大喜，传给身边的美人和侍从看，左右都高呼万岁。相如看出秦王无意偿城，上前说璧有小毛病要指给秦王看，拿到璧便退立倚柱，怒发上冲冠，当面斥责秦王，放话：大王若一定要逼我，「臣頭今與璧倶碎於柱矣」；直到此时才「持其璧睨柱，欲以撃柱」。秦王怕他砸碎，连忙道歉，召来主管官员查看地图，指着说从这里过去的十五座城给赵。相如判断这不过是做样子，城根本拿不到，于是说和氏璧是天下共传之宝，赵王送来前斋戒五日，秦王也该斋戒五日，设九宾于廷，他才敢献璧。秦王答应了，把他安置在广成传舍。相如断定秦王即便斋戒也一定违约，就让随从穿上粗布衣，把璧揣在怀里，从小路逃走，送回赵国。等再次上廷，他把话摊开：秦自缪公以来二十多位国君，没有一位说话算数；璧已送回赵国，「臣知欺大王之罪當誅，臣請就湯鑊」。秦王与群臣相视而嘻，左右有人要把他拉下去，秦王最终说，杀了相如也得不到璧，反而断了秦赵之好，不如以礼相待送他回去，「卒廷見相如，畢禮而歸之」。

At the Qin court the king received Lin Xiangru in the Zhang Terrace, was delighted with the jade, and passed it around to his ladies and attendants, who all cried long life to him. Lin Xiangru saw he had no intention of paying. He said the gem had a small flaw he would point out, took it back and stood against a pillar, his hair bristling with anger, and denounced the king, warning that if the king insisted on pressing him, his head and the jade would be smashed together against the pillar. Only then did he stand holding the jade with his eyes on the pillar, ready to bring it down. The alarmed king apologised, summoned the officials concerned to consult the map and pointed out fifteen cities for Zhao. Lin Xiangru judged this mere show. The Heshi jade was a treasure the whole world talked of, he said; the king of Zhao had fasted five days before sending it, and the king of Qin should fast five days and hold the nine-fold ceremony at court before he would dare present it. The king agreed and lodged him at the Guangcheng hostel. Sure that the king would break his word even after fasting, Lin Xiangru had a follower put on coarse clothes, hide the jade in his robe and take it home to Zhao by back roads. At the next audience he laid it out: in more than twenty reigns since Duke Mu, Qin had never kept a firm agreement; the jade was already back in Zhao; he knew that deceiving the king was a crime deserving death, and he asked to be sent to the cauldron. The king and his ministers looked at one another and laughed wryly. Some attendants moved to drag him out, but the king reasoned that killing him would not bring back the jade and would end good relations with Zhao. In the end he received Lin Xiangru at court with full ceremony and sent him home.
回国以后，因相如功大，拜为上卿，位在廉颇之右。廉颇的话说得很白：「我爲趙將，有攻城野戰之大功，而藺相如徒以口舌爲勞，而位居我上，且相如素賤人，吾羞，不忍爲之下。」并且公开宣言：「我見相如，必辱之。」

Back home, Lin Xiangru, for his great service, was made shangqing, ranked above Lian Po. Lian Po put it plainly: I am the general of Zhao, with great merit from storming cities and fighting in the field, while Lin Xiangru has labored only with his tongue and sits above me; and he has always been a man of low station. I am ashamed, and I cannot bear to stand beneath him. Then he declared openly: when I set eyes on Lin Xiangru, I will humiliate him.
相如听说后，不肯与他相会。每逢朝会，常称病不去，不想同廉颇争位次的先后。出门远远望见廉颇，他就让自己的车避开躲起来。

Lin Xiangru, hearing of it, refused to meet him. At court audiences he would often plead illness rather than jostle with Lian Po over precedence. When he did go out and caught sight of Lian Po in the distance, he turned his carriage aside and hid.
相如坚决把他们留住，反问一句：你们看廉将军和秦王比，谁更厉害？舍人说，廉将军当然不如秦王。相如说，以秦王那样的威势，我敢当廷呵斥他、羞辱他的群臣，我再没出息，难道单单怕一个廉将军？「顧吾念之，彊秦之所以不敢加兵於趙者，徒以吾兩人在也。今兩虎共鬥，其勢不倶生。」我所以这样做，「以先國家之急而後私讎也」。

Lin Xiangru firmly refused to let them leave, and put a question back: how does General Lian compare with the king of Qin? Not his equal, they said. With all the king of Qin's might, said Lin Xiangru, I rebuked him to his face at court and shamed his ministers. Incompetent as I am, would I be afraid of General Lian alone? But consider: the reason mighty Qin has not dared to send its armies against Zhao is only that the two of us are still here. If two tigers fight, the way things stand, they cannot both live. I do this because I put the state's urgent need first and my private enmity second.
廉颇听说了这番话，「肉袒負荊」，由宾客引路，到相如门前谢罪，说「鄙賤之人，不知將軍寬之至此也」。两人终于和好，成为刎颈之交。当年廉颇东攻齐，破其一军；两年后廉颇又伐齐，攻下幾邑；再过三年，他攻魏国的防陵、安阳，都攻了下来；又过四年，相如也带兵攻齐，到平邑而罢。

When Lian Po heard this, he stripped off his shirt, took up a bundle of thorns on his back, and came through guests to Lin Xiangru's gate to apologize: a crude and lowly man, he said, who did not know how far the general's generosity went. In the end the two were reconciled and became friends who would die for each other. That same year Lian Po struck east against Qi and broke one of its armies. Two years on he campaigned against Qi again and took Ji. Three years after that he stormed Wei's Fangling and Anyang. Four years later Lin Xiangru himself led an army against Qi and stopped at Pingyi.

相如的避让也不是单纯的忍。他给舍人的理由不是廉颇不值一提，而是一个盘面判断：「彊秦之所以不敢加兵於趙者，徒以吾兩人在也」——强秦不敢动手，只因为我们两个还在。作者认为，他把争执从谁功劳大，换成了赵国安危系于两人并存。同时，避让用的是称病、让路这类不上台面的动作，原文只记了称病、引车避匿，没有记他公开回应廉颇；一种解释是，这样就没有把对方逼到必须立刻表态的位置。一种解释是，这正是给对方留的台阶：羞辱的话是公开说出去的，化解则不是在朝堂上当众进行的（作者解释），廉颇要回头，不必先当众收回自己的话。

Lin Xiangru's yielding was not simple endurance either. The reason he gave his retainers was not that Lian Po was beneath notice, but a judgment about the whole board: the reason mighty Qin has not dared to send its armies against Zhao is only that the two of us are still here. The author's reading is that he shifted the dispute from whose merit was greater to the fact that Zhao's safety rested on both men surviving together. And the yielding itself used offstage moves - pleading illness, turning his carriage aside - and the record notes no public reply to Lian Po. On one reading, that kept the other man from being forced to take a stand on the spot. One reading is that this was precisely the ramp built for a retreat. The insult had been spoken in the open; the undoing did not take place before the court (the author's interpretation), so Lian Po could turn back without first withdrawing his words before an audience.
同一篇列传里，认错的动作出现过两次。早年缪贤有罪，相如给他出的主意是「肉袒伏斧質請罪」；后来廉颇上门，做的是「肉袒負荊」。两者都是脱去上衣、把身体交出去的姿势。不能断言廉颇知道前一桩事或受其影响（作者提示，非原文所述）。另外，《史记》所记的那段权衡用的是另一套语言：先说清「曲在趙」还是「曲在秦」，把理亏的一方安排到对方。太史公的评语是「退而讓頗，名重太山」——退让，反而把名望抬到了泰山那么高。

Within the same biography the gesture of admitting fault appears twice. Lin Xiangru's advice to Miao Xian was to strip and lie on the block to ask pardon; when Lian Po came to the gate, he came stripped to the waist with thorns on his back. Both are postures of baring the body and handing it over. One cannot say that Lian Po knew of the earlier case or was influenced by it; the parallel is the author's observation, not something the text states. The weighing of options recorded in the Shiji uses a different grammar: first settle where the wrong will lie, with Zhao or with Qin, and arrange for it to fall on the other side. The Grand Historian's verdict: he stepped back and yielded to Lian Po, and his name came to weigh as much as Mount Tai.
还要说，作者认为，一次认错未必改变了廉颇的脾气。后来赵孝成王去世，悼襄王即位，派乐乘去替代廉颇，廉颇怒而攻乐乘，乐乘跑掉，廉颇便投奔魏国大梁。另据记载，他自长平免归失势时门客散尽，复用为将时门客又回来，门客还说「天下以市道交」，有势就来、无势就走本是常理。把这些放在一起，不是要给谁下道德评语，只是说明：相如门前那次负荆谢罪见于本篇《史记》记载，它也没有把一个人从此改写。

The author's reading is that one apology did not necessarily remake Lian Po's temper. When King Xiaocheng of Zhao died, his successor King Daoxiang sent Le Cheng to replace Lian Po; Lian Po, enraged, attacked Le Cheng, who fled, and Lian Po then went over to Daliang in Wei. According to another passage, when he was dismissed after Changping and lost power, his retainers had all left, and when he was made a general again they came back; one of them told him that the world conducts its friendships on market terms (in translation): people come when you have power and leave when you do not. None of this is a moral verdict on anyone. It only shows that the apology at Lin Xiangru's gate is recorded in this chapter of the Shiji, and that it did not rewrite the man from that day on.

删去“the highest ministerial rank”，“the top rank”改为“the rank of shangqing”。中文原本没有“最高”之说，未改动。
删去英文本段多出的“his courage known to every state”，与中文对齐。该事实已在 hook.0 中写到。
“shimen”改为“sheren”，并删去证据之外的“living in the household”，改为“a retainer in the service of Miao Xian”。
删去带引号的译文和“as the phrase went”，改为不加引号的转述，并注明“to paraphrase the source”。中文「肉袒伏斧質請罪」与证据逐字一致，保留。

删去“相如出使前”和“he said”的归属，改为“《史记》记有这样的权衡”/“The Shiji records this weighing of options”。结尾改为不带因果的“相如奉璧出使秦国”，“使臣奉璧”可为依据。

节选正文能证明的是：说话人为缪贤（其舍人即相如），对象为赵王，所讲内容涉及相如；正文并未直接写出“举荐”。为稳妥起见，改为“缪贤向赵王提起相如，讲了自己的一桩旧事”，英文同步。
